correctness.rationale: Fourier coefficients on the dual lattice equal (up to fundamental-cell volume) Fourier coefficients of the locally finite lattice-periodized compactly supported mixture; all vanishing means periodization zero a.e. Fix any one sphere boundary S_j. Only finitely many lattice translates of the finite family intersect a compact tubular neighborhood of S_j. If none is identical in parameter class, each other sphere intersects S_j in at most a proper codimension-one subsphere, so d>=2 provides an open patch of S_j free of all other boundaries. The alleged zero periodization has a jump exactly a_j across that patch, forcing a_j=0. For d=1, the distribution derivative on R/sZ is the summed signed endpoint delta measure. Vanishing derivative gives an a.e. constant; the integral over one cell is sum 2a_jr_j, so these two independent conditions are necessary and sufficient. A length-s interval shifted by a nonlattice amount supplies sharp aliasing. Independently computed a planar six-disk 81-frequency matrix with rank 6 and minimum singular 0.2968204, and checked interval periodization; such finite checks do not establish all-lattice uniqueness.
